title: Removing the defender
objectives: Identify the one piece actually holding a position together before deciding a piece is safe
Capture an undefended defender to win the piece it was guarding a move later
Deflect a defender away with a check instead of capturing it directly

steps.text: Sometimes a piece looks safe only because of a single defender — find that defender, remove it (by capturing it or forcing it away), and the piece it was guarding falls next. This is 'removing the defender': instead of attacking the valuable piece directly, you attack the much less glamorous piece that's actually holding everything together.

steps.prompt: Removing the defender only works if capturing the defender itself wins material outright.

feedback.default: It's even stronger when capturing the defender wins material on its own — but it also works as an even or slightly costly trade, as long as what you win afterward (by capturing the now-undefended piece) makes the whole sequence worth it.

steps.successExplanation: Right — the defender doesn't have to be a free capture on its own; the whole point is what the sequence wins overall.

steps.prompt: The rook on d8 is defended only by the knight on f7. Capture the knight first — it's undefended and clears the way.

hints.text: Before attacking the rook directly, find the one piece that's actually defending it.
The knight is the rook's only defender, and it's undefended itself.
Bxf7 wins the knight for free — and that knight was the rook's only defender, so the rook falls next move with nothing able to save it.

feedback.default: That doesn't win the defender. Find the piece that's actually guarding the rook on d8, and capture it.

steps.successExplanation: Bxf7 wins the knight for free. That knight was the rook's only defender, so the rook is next — removing the defender turned one small win into a much bigger one.

steps.prompt: One trade later, the rook's defender is gone. Capture the rook.

hints.text: Nothing defends the rook anymore — take it.
Your rook already lines up with it.
Rxd8 wins the rook for free. Once its only defender was removed, it was never actually safe.

feedback.default: That doesn't win the rook. Check whether anything defends d8 now — then capture.

steps.successExplanation: Rxd8 wins the rook for free. Once its only defender was removed, the rook itself was never actually safe — this is the payoff of removing the defender.

steps.prompt: Give check to force the king away — it's the only thing defending the bishop on f7.

hints.text: You don't have to capture a defender to remove it — forcing it to move works just as well. What defends the bishop right now?
The king is the bishop's only defender — force it to move.
Re4+ forces the king to move. Wherever it goes, it can no longer guard f7 the way it did — the bishop is yours next move.

feedback.default: That doesn't remove the defender. The king is the bishop's only guard — find the move that forces it away from that job.

steps.successExplanation: Re4+ forces the king to move. Wherever it goes, it can no longer guard f7 the way it did — the bishop is yours next move. Forcing a defender away works just as well as capturing it, and doesn't require the defender itself to be undefended.

steps.prompt: Before capturing a piece that looks defended, what should 'removing the defender' lead you to check?
options: Whether the defended piece is worth capturing at all
What piece is actually doing the defending, and whether it can be captured or forced away first
Whether the position has any checks available

feedback.default: Removing the defender is a two-step plan: identify the specific piece that's defending, then deal with that piece — by capturing it or forcing it to move — before going after the real target.

steps.successExplanation: Right — identify the actual defender first, then deal with it, before going after what it's protecting.

steps.summary: Removing the defender means identifying the one piece actually holding a position together, then dealing with it — either by capturing it directly (especially if it's undefended itself) or by forcing it away with a check or a bigger threat. Once the defender is gone, the piece it was guarding is yours. Always ask: what is actually defending this, and can I get rid of that instead of attacking the target head-on?
